clue.text: Property located in a large vessel

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the other here

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a large vessel
located means set, as a house is set on a hill

explanation.surface: Someone's valuables turn up stowed aboard a big ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Located' reads as a link but supplies letters; SS (steamship) is a standard crossword shorthand for a big ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are possessions or holdings, the things a person owns.

clue.text: Evaluation of top artist is accepted by a friend

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: accepted by means the artist and is go inside the friend word

parts.note: a pal is a friend
PRA is President of the Royal Academy, the top British artist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A leading painter's work is welcomed by a companion as an assessment.
explanation.walkthrough: PRA, President of the Royal Academy, is a crossword convention for a top artist.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal is an assessment of worth or quality.

clue.text: A contest held by Poles for an Arab

indicators.note: held by means the contest sits between the poles

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
taken as written
a race is a contest

explanation.surface: A competition hosted in Poland for a Middle Eastern visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' are the compass points S and N, not people from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracen was the medieval European name for a Muslim or Arab, especially in the Crusades.

clue.text: Innocent bystander violently hit on way to social

indicators.note: violently suggests the word hit is thrown about, rearranged

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
a social is a party, an informal gathering

explanation.surface: A passer-by is attacked on the road to a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A third party is someone outside a dispute or deal, an uninvolved person.

clue.text: Fellow sailor finally becomes joint first officer

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word becomes

parts.note: the hip is a joint of the body
the mate is the first officer on a merchant ship

explanation.surface: A crewman ends up sharing command as second-in-charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like an adjective (shared) but is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipmate is a companion aboard the same vessel, a crewmate.

clue.text: Clumsy man he'd had replaced

indicators.note: replaced suggests the letters of man he'd had are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A clumsy fellow, the man she once had, was swapped out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ham-handed means awkward or heavy-handed with things.

clue.text: A small glass? Forty would be grand!

explanation.surface: A tot of drink, and forty of them would be lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a pony is £25 and a grand is £1000, so forty ponies make a grand.
explanation.definitionFit: A pony is a small measure of beer or spirits; it is also slang for twenty-five pounds sterling.

clue.text: Man improperly receiving acting award? It means the opposite

indicators.note: receiving means the scrambled man holds the acting award inside
improperly suggests the letters of man are set out wrongly

parts.note: a Tony is an American theatre award

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly given a prize for acting, which is the reverse of what was meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Improperly' scrambles the man; the Tony Awards honour Broadway theatre, so 'acting award' is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word of contrary meaning, as hot to cold.

clue.text: London costermonger quietly departs ahead of time

indicators.note: departs says the letter for quietly leaves the costermonger word

parts.note: a pearly king or queen is a London street trader in a suit sewn with pearl buttons
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A London barrow boy slips away quietly before the appointed hour.
explanation.walkthrough: A costermonger is a London street seller of fruit and vegetables; pearlies are their ceremonial leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: Early means before the expected or usual hour.

clue.text: Familiar author soon identified

explanation.surface: A well-known writer is quickly named.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Identified' is a link: the writer is known by that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anonymous is credited on many works, making it a familiar byline; anon is also archaic for shortly.

clue.text: Helping a lot?

explanation.definitionFit: A helping is a serving of food; a lot, as in one's lot in life, is one's share or fate.

clue.text: Clergyman deprived of one church

indicators.note: deprived of says the clergyman word loses a letter

parts.note: a minister is a clergyman
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A vicar is stripped of his only parish.
explanation.definitionFit: A minster is a large or important church, such as York's cathedral.

clue.text: Canal cited mistakenly as non-essential

indicators.note: mistakenly suggests the letters of canal cited are set out wrongly, rearranged

explanation.surface: A waterway mentioned in error is dismissed as unimportant.
explanation.definitionFit: Accidental can mean incidental or secondary, not of the essence of a thing.

clue.text: It's just part of a Byron lyric

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a quotation as merely a fragment of a Byron poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Only and just are synonyms: 'it's only me' means 'it's just me'.

clue.text: Versatile type taking run with a couple of students

parts.note: taken as written
L is a learner, so two of them give LL
a rounder is a run scored in the British bat-and-ball game rounders

explanation.surface: A capable all-rounder scoring a run alongside two learners.
explanation.walkthrough: Rounders is a British children's game like baseball; a complete circuit scores a rounder.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-rounder is someone skilled in many fields, as a cricketer who bats and bowls.

clue.text: Artificial aid available for a tanner?

definitions.text: Artificial aid available for a tanner?

parts.words: Artificial aid available for a tanner?
parts.note: a tanner sounds like a leather worker or an old British sixpence coin, but here is someone browning their skin indoors

explanation.surface: Something manufactured that could be had for sixpence.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was slang for the old British sixpence, so the clue seems to ask what could be bought cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunlamp gives ultraviolet light to tan the skin without sunshine.

clue.text: Church people going into fragment of old manuscript

indicators.note: going into means the church and people are placed inside the fragment word

parts.note: a part is a fragment
men are people

explanation.surface: Congregants gather in a scrap of an ancient scroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Parchment is prepared animal skin used for writing, and a document written on it.

clue.text: Obscure scholar covering the French problem

indicators.note: covering means the first word wraps around the French article

parts.note: obscure means dim, unclear
le is French for the
an MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: A puzzling academic hides the French language's problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a hard choice or predicament.

clue.text: Day's rules — broken without doubt!

indicators.note: broken suggests the letters of day's rules are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: The day's regulations are certainly being flouted.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuredly means certainly, surely.

clue.text: "'Tis the voice of the —', I heard him declare" (Carroll)

definitions.text: "'Tis the voice of the —', I heard him declare" (Carroll)

parts.words: "'Tis the voice of the —', I heard him declare" (Carroll)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from the poem recited by Alice in Lewis Carroll's Wonderland, parodying Isaac Watts's 'Tis the voice of the sluggard'

explanation.surface: A line of Lewis Carroll's verse with one word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Alice's Adventures in Wonderland the parody poem begins with the shellfish's voice, replacing Watts's sluggard.

clue.text: Major transaction? I'm not impressed

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs at an important business arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a large business agreement; said sarcastically, it dismisses something as unimportant.

clue.text: Sounds like a city's devices for securing prisoners

indicators.note: sounds like says the city word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: Derby is an English city, and British speakers say it 'darby'

explanation.surface: Something about how a city's restraints for inmates are pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: Darbies is old slang for handcuffs, fetters for holding captives.

clue.text: The incentive for a single legislator in France and America

parts.note: a single is one, I
an MP is a Member of Parliament
et is French for and
US is America

explanation.surface: A motivation for one lawmaker in both France and the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In France' modifies 'and', giving its French form.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is a driving force or stimulus to act.

clue.text: Cloak and sort of shirt rejected in the past

parts.note: a T-shirt is a sort of shirt, giving T

indicators.note: rejected means the phrase for in the past is turned back to front

parts.note: ago means in the past

explanation.surface: An outfit of cape and a certain shirt, discarded long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A toga was the loose outer garment worn by Roman citizens, a kind of mantle.

clue.text: It is forbidden to set about a native Australian

indicators.note: set about means the word to is placed around the native Australian term

parts.note: taken as written
Abo is a dated, now offensive, word for an Aboriginal Australian

explanation.surface: It is not allowed to attack an indigenous Australian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set about' looks like 'attack', but it tells the solver to put one piece round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Taboo means prohibited by custom or social rule.

clue.text: Way in which garment is put on society sportsperson

parts.note: how means the way in which something is done
a jumper is a knitted garment, a sweater

explanation.surface: A fashion tip on how a top should be worn by a society figure.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater; 'is put on' places it after the society and way pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A showjumper is a rider who competes at leaping fences in an arena.

clue.text: Old politician's husband wearing toupee

indicators.note: wearing means the husband abbreviation is placed under the hairpiece word

parts.note: a wig is a hairpiece, of which a toupee is one

explanation.surface: A veteran statesman's spouse sports a hairpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Whigs were a British party of the 17th to 19th centuries, forerunners of the Liberals.

clue.text: E.g. Shakespeare's determined intention

explanation.surface: The Bard had a resolute purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: William Shakespeare is known as Will; will also means firm resolve or purpose.

clue.text: A course taken directly by the workers

definitions.text: A course taken directly by the workers

parts.words: A course taken directly by the workers
parts.note: a straight route, read also as the path taken by worker bees flying home to the hive

explanation.surface: Employees take the most direct route.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees are said to fly straight back to the hive, hence the phrase for a direct route.

clue.text: Reportedly accused in writing

indicators.note: reportedly says we hear a word that is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: indicted means formally accused of a crime

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have been charged by letter.
explanation.walkthrough: INDICTED is said with a silent C, so it sounds like the answer. The definition reads as 'put in writing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To indite is an old word meaning to compose or put down on paper.

clue.text: Officer reluctant to carry the Italian waterproof

indicators.note: to carry means the officer abbreviation holds the Italian article inside

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding
il is Italian for the
loth means unwilling or reluctant

explanation.surface: An officer is unwilling to transport the Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilcloth is cotton treated with oil to make it shed water, used for tablecloths.

clue.text: High-spirited female with chancy following

indicators.note: following says the chancy word comes after the female abbreviation

parts.note: chancy means risky, uncertain

explanation.surface: A lively woman with a dangerous man in pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisky describes a lively, playful mood.
